Subject: ENGLISH

Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fictional and Non-Fictional
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fictional and Non-Fictional, part of TECHNOLOGY: SCIENTIFIC INNOVATIONS Suggested Vocabulary engineer, computer scien in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you obtain the general idea of what a text is about? 2. Why is it important to read many books?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  Select a reading text from a varied collection of materials or library,  Preview the table of contents from a book, find the required information, and answer oral questions,  In purposive groups, skim a text to obtain the gist or general idea,  In purposive groups scan a text to obtain specific information,  In purposive groups select a reading text (1251-1500 words),  Use a dictionary to look up the meaning of unfamiliar words. Learners who may not perform the practical task could point/ carry out the task orally while being offered physical support 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  Select a reading text from a varied collection of materials or library,  Preview the table of contents from a book, find the required information, and answer oral questions,  In purposive groups, skim a text to obtain the gist or general idea,  In purposive groups scan a text to obtain specific information,  In purposive groups select a reading text (1251-1500 words),  Use a dictionary to look up the meaning of unfamiliar words. Learners who may not perform the practical task could point/ carry out the task orally while being offered physical support 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fictional and Non-Fictional together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Learning to Learn: The learner’s ability to acquire the skill of selecting and reading a variety of texts is enhanced as they

select, read and summarise texts.

 Collaboration: The learner’s ability to work with others harmoniously is boosted as they observe the rules of engagement

while sharing a summary of the text he or she has read.

Values:
Respect is inculcated in the learner as they display patience while writing a summary of a text he or she has read and sharing it

with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Critical Thinking: The learner acquires the skills of critical thinking while skimming a text to obtain the gist or general idea.

Link to other Subjects

Extensive reading is necessary as learners carry out research while doing assignments and general reading in Social Studies.
